sentences.text: Dr. Khuzema Kapadia, learned counsel for the Petitioner   Shri Surendra Gupta, learned Govt. Advocate for the resp Shri Nilesh Patel, learned counsel for the Respondent [R-1][OBJ].
Heard on I.A. No.635/2024, which is an application filed under Section 389(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 for suspension of sentence on behalf of appellant-Rewaram.
2. Appellant-Rewaram has been convicted under Sections 368 of IPC, 1860 and sentenced to undergo 07 years R.I. with fine and default stipulation.

3. Also Heard on I.A. No.2464/2024, application under Section389(1) of Cr.P.C for suspension of sentence moved on behalf of appellant Manish.
4.

Appellant Manish has been convicted for offence under Sections 366, 376(2)(n), 5(j)(ii)(6) of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and sentenced to undergo 7 years, 10 years and 10 years R.I. with fine and default stipulation.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for the appellants submitted that there are omissions and contradictions in the statement of the prosecution witnesses and the trial Court has committed an error in appreciating the evidence and convicting the appellants.

It is further submitted that the prosecutrix has compromised the matter and married appellant Manish and she has also filed her no objection,
therefore, he prayed that sentence of the appellants be also suspended.
There is no likelihood final hearing of this appeal.
Hence, remaining jail sentence of the appellants may be suspended.
6. Learned Government Advocate for the respondent/State opposes the prayer and prays for its rejection.
7. Prosecutrix is present in person, she has been duly identified by her counsel and she has submitted her no objection.

sentences.text: Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case and submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties, no objection of the prosecutrix, I find it to be a fit case to suspend the custodial sentence of the appellants.

9. Accordingly, both the applications stands allowed and it is directed that the execution of jail sentence awarded to the appellants shall remain suspended till final disposal of the appeal, subject to the depositing the fine amount, if any, and upon furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees fifty thousand) each with one solvent surety each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for their appearance before Registry of this Court on 22.04.2024 and on such other dates as may be fixed by the Registry in this regard.
10.
Accordingly, IA Nos.635/2024 and 2464/2024 stands allowed and disposed of.

11. List the matter for final hearing in due course.
